findings.title: `float: right` on small-action button no longer works now that `.small-action` is a flex container
findings.body: `.small-action` was turned into a flex container (`@include flexbox()` at line 264). Float is ignored on flex items, so the `button { float: right; }` rule at line 309 has no effect anymore and the action button (e.g. undo/delete on small post actions) will sit immediately after `.small-action-desc` instead of being pushed to the right edge. To keep the previous layout the button needs `margin-left: auto` (or the container needs `justify-content: space-between`). The same applies to `.topic-avatar { float: left; }` (line 270), which is now dead.

findings.title: Right-alignment of header `.panel` breaks in browsers that only support the legacy box model
findings.body: `.contents` is now laid out with the `flexbox()` mixin, which also emits the legacy `display: -webkit-box` / `-moz-box` fallbacks. Those old box-model implementations do not honour `margin-left: auto` for pushing an item to the end of the line, and the previous `float: right` on `.panel` (plus `float: left` on `.title`) was removed in this diff. In any engine that falls back to `-webkit-box`/`-moz-box` (old Android/iOS WebKit, Firefox < 22) the header panel with the user icons/search will be rendered left-aligned next to the title instead of right-aligned, i.e. a visibly broken header. Either keep a float fallback or drop the legacy `box` fallbacks from the mixin.

findings.title: `align-items` mixin emits legacy properties that reject the modern keyword values
findings.body: The mixin blindly maps the argument onto `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align`. Those legacy properties accept `start`/`end`/`center`/`baseline`/`stretch`, not `flex-start`/`flex-end`. So `@include align-items(flex-start)` silently produces invalid legacy declarations and the legacy-only engines fall back to the default `stretch`, producing a different layout than intended. Also `-ms-align-items` is not a real property (IE10 uses only `-ms-flex-align`), and `-moz-box-align` is missing even though `flexbox()` emits `display: -moz-box`, so Firefox's legacy box path gets no alignment at all.

findings.title: `order` mixin mixes 1-based legacy ordinal groups with 0-based `order`
findings.body: `-webkit-box-ordinal-group`/`-moz-box-ordinal-group` are 1-based (default 1) while the standard `order` property is 0-based (default 0), and `box-ordinal-group: 0` is invalid. As a result `@include order(0)` emits an invalid legacy declaration, and `@include order(1)` makes the element tie with siblings that have no order set in legacy engines, while in modern engines it is placed after them. Any mixin consumer therefore gets different sibling ordering depending on the engine; the legacy value should be `$val + 1`.
